speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent, and I am here to evaluate your child for the cause of systemic hypertension. To begin, could you please tell me the patient's age and gender?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Since this is a well-child visit, could you tell me what the current blood pressure reading is, and do you know if it has been elevated on previous visits?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see that the blood pressure was elevated in the right arm. To help narrow down the cause, could you tell me if the blood pressure was also measured in the left arm or legs, and if so, were those readings different? Additionally, has anyone ever noted a weak pulse in his legs or a murmur on his chest?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Born full term with an uneventful neonatal period. Social history: Patient attends kindergarten. Lives with parents and one younger sibling. No exposure to tobacco smoke.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The mother provided social history but did not answer my specific questions regarding blood pressure in other limbs or physical exam findings. I need to know if there is a discrepancy in blood pressure between the arms and legs, or if there are radio-femoral delays, to suspect coarctation of the aorta or other vascular anomalies.

Can you confirm if the blood pressure was measured in the left arm and both legs, and were those readings lower than the right arm? Also, did the doctor find a weak or delayed pulse in the feet compared to the arms?

speaker: Patient
text: All systems review is essentially negative as reported by the mother.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the history is non-contributory, I will proceed with a physical examination. I am palpating for radio-femoral delays and auscultating for systolic murmurs, particularly over the left infraclavicular area and back. REQUEST TEST: ECHO_DOPPLER

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal.

speaker: Doctor
text: The echocardiogram confirms a narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery, which aligns with the elevated right arm blood pressure. This finding is diagnostic for coarctation of the aorta. DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the aorta
